tags: HistGradientBoostingClassifier, Gradient Boosting, Tree-based Model, Ensemble Learning
description: The approach utilizes a HistGradientBoostingClassifier configured with constrained depth, leaf nodes, and L2 regularization to classify physical activity types. To ensure generalization to unseen subjects, user-identifying columns are dropped prior to training.
insights: Dropping subject and user ID columns prevents the model from memorizing specific individuals, which is essential for the dataset's per-user split. Additionally, applying 1st and 99th percentile clipping on numerical features prevents transient sensor glitches from skewing the model's decision boundaries.

tags: LightGBM, Gradient Boosting, Multiclass Classification, Decision Trees
description: A LightGBM multiclass classifier trained with 250 boosting rounds, a learning rate of 0.05, and native categorical feature handling to predict six distinct physical activity types.
insights: The model utilizes a max depth of 8 and a feature fraction of 0.8 to mitigate overfitting on user-stratified splits, achieving a test macro F1 score of approximately 0.60. Native categorical encoding simplifies preprocessing while preserving relationships in demographic and device metadata.

tags: ExtraTreesClassifier, RandomForestClassifier, HistGradientBoostingClassifier, Soft Voting Ensemble, Feature Engineering, Class Weighting
description: The solution constructs physiological interaction and ratio features tailored to physical activity intensities before training a soft-voting ensemble of ExtraTrees, RandomForest, and HistGradientBoosting classifiers. Explicit class balancing and sample weights are incorporated into the models to maintain representation across all activity levels.
insights: Engineering normalized domain features like MET proxies, cardiac cost, and heart rate relative to resting rate helps the model generalize across unseen participants without relying on demographic memorization. Explicit sample weighting across tree models prevents minority classes (such as distinct running MET intensities) from collapsing during probability estimation.

tags: HistGradientBoostingClassifier, Feature Engineering, GroupKFold, Class Weighting, Physiological Metrics
description: The solution utilizes a HistGradientBoostingClassifier trained with balanced sample weighting on newly engineered physiological and interaction features. Raw demographic variables are dropped post-feature creation to prevent subject-level memorization and improve out-of-subject activity prediction.
insights: Grouping StratifiedGroupKFold validation using composite demographic identifiers prevents data leakage from identical subjects. Replacing raw demographic attributes with derived domain features (e.g., BMI, heart rate reserve ratio, and step-intensity interactions) enhances generalization across unseen participants.

tags: HistGradientBoosting, ExtraTrees, RandomForest, Ensemble, Post-Processing Calibration, Feature Engineering
description: The approach uses a 3-model ensemble combining HistGradientBoosting, ExtraTrees, and RandomForest classifiers evaluated via StratifiedGroupKFold on participant demographic proxies. Predicted class probabilities are refined using a post-hoc bounded probability multiplier calibration step to optimize joint Accuracy and F1-macro scores.
insights: Constructing physiological domain features (Tanaka HRR%, Mifflin-St Jeor METs, BMI, and stride dynamics) while explicitly dropping raw demographic identifiers prevents participant memorization and improves generalization to unseen subjects. Bounded class probability adjustment effectively addresses class imbalance and improves macro-F1 across rare activity types.

tags: HistGradientBoosting, RandomForest, Ensemble Blend, Feature Engineering, Dampened Class Weights, StratifiedGroupKFold
description: The approach uses a weighted ensemble of HistGradientBoosting (80%) and Random Forest (20%) trained on domain-engineered physiological and biomechanical features. Raw demographic features and direct participant identifiers are removed to improve generalization to unseen individuals evaluated via StratifiedGroupKFold.
insights: Engineering normalized physiological metrics—such as percentage of estimated maximum heart rate, steps per calorie, and calories per basal metabolic rate—allows models to generalize effectively across participants without memorizing physical attributes. Dampening balanced sample weights with a square-root power transformation provides a optimal trade-off between macro F1-score and overall accuracy.

tags: LightGBM, Gradient Boosting, Stratified Group K-Fold, Balanced Class Weights, Baseline Model
description: The solution employs a standard LightGBM classifier with balanced class weights trained directly on raw tabular sensor features. To prevent identity leakage and simulate unseen participants, it evaluates performance using 5-fold StratifiedGroupKFold grouped by demographic feature proxies.
insights: Creating a participant proxy by combining demographic features (age, gender, height, weight) provides a valid grouped cross-validation strategy aligned with unseen participant evaluation. The baseline reliance on balanced class weights helps maintain macro-F1 performance across rare physical activity classes.

tags: HistGradientBoosting, Feature Engineering, StratifiedGroupKFold, Gradient Boosting
description: The approach utilizes a HistGradientBoostingClassifier tuned with balanced class weights and L2 regularization to classify physical activity levels. Cross-validation is conducted using StratifiedGroupKFold based on demographic-derived participant proxies to evaluate generalization to unseen individuals.
insights: Engineered physiological features such as BMI, Heart Rate Reserve, and stride length proxies provide robust context for activity tracking. Additionally, motion-cardiovascular interaction terms (e.g., steps multiplied by normalized heart rate) help separate distinct running intensity classes, while device-encoded interaction terms adjust for sensor biases across brands.

tags: RandomForestClassifier, GroupKFold, Class-Weight Balancing, Probability Calibration, Ensembling
description: The solution trains standard and class-balanced ('balanced_subsample') Random Forests using 5-fold GroupKFold cross-validation grouped by demographic features. Out-of-fold predictions are blended and calibrated using a prior-exponent power adjustment to optimize F1-macro and accuracy across unseen subjects.
insights: Reconstructing subject groups from identical demographic metadata (age, gender, height, weight) effectively prevents data leakage across individual participants during cross-validation. Post-hoc probability calibration combined with blended class-weighting improves decision thresholding for minority and confused activity classes.
